TIL three alleged instigators, masked and carrying rocks, at a peaceful protest in Quebec were undercover police. Astute protesters noticed the boots they were wearing were the same as police.

This happens everywhere, including the US. There have been many confirmed undercover police injected into protests. They tried it during the Hong Kong protest but the people there to actually protest wouldn't allow the instigators to loot or riot and did a pretty good job at keeping it all peaceful, which is why you never heard anybody demonizing the whole movement.

Turning a peaceful protest into a riot/lootfest is the easiest way to remove all credibility from peoples' grievances and gives you a perfect excuse to escalate force. As soon as the first window is broken it stops being a protest and starts being a riot. The issues disappear from view and all we talk about is how these people are acting like animals, never mind why.

People think it's a coincidence that all of these protests end up in riots but it's definitely not. Think about all the shit you read on the internet about Baltimore or St Louis when it was happening. As soon as the protests went from peaceful to riots, people stopped talking about the issue and started focusing on the people. It wasn't about police brutality any more, it was about people stealing shit. All of a sudden, we went from a real issue to something that people think was comparable to the riots after a bad soccer game. Half the people outraged by the rioting had no idea there were four days of peaceful protests before suddenly things got violent in Baltimore.

Sprinkle in some very aggressive media bias that twists the truth at will to generate ratings with absolutely no consequences even when they're caught red-handed and you've got a pretty nice recipe to dissolve public dissonance whenever it crops up.

Welp, the people planted at protests are mainly there to get the mob mentality kick started, or blend in with the crowd so that they can meet other people who intend to start trouble. It's a way to catch people. But can we give them the benefit of the doubt?

Windows 8 was a terrible mess, because the built the UI from the cell phone up to the PC, in accordance to the smart phone market exploding.
